A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AsymKV and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Appendices A–C can be matched across versions; v2 adds a checklist and Appendices D–E.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, compression and efficiency experiments, merge-strategy ablations, and empirical analyses of key-value asymmetry.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds LongBench results comparing additional baselines on Llama3-8B-Instruct in Appendix D.

M1.justification: Adjacent-key selection, Fisher-based key merging, value summation with cardinality normalization, chunked compression, and selective gradient computation remain unchanged. The expanded memory discussion documents the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain LongBench, LongBenchV2, TopicRet, and the ShareGPT, QASPER, and MultiFieldQA analyses. Appendix D reuses LongBench; its additional model does not introduce new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix D and Table 5 add evaluated comparisons against SnapKV, PyramidKV, TOVA, D2O, and L2-norm, alongside the existing baselines. This substantially broadens the actual comparator set beyond methods merely cited in v1.

E3.justification: Appendix D introduces a Llama3-8B-Instruct evaluation with max_length=2048. This supplements the retained Llama3.1-8B and other model settings; existing experiments retain their reported cache budgets, chunk sizes, and procedures.

E4.justification: The compression-ratio study, merge-strategy ablation, and cross-model/dataset asymmetry analyses are retained unchanged. Appendix D adds benchmark comparisons, while the new regularization discussion supplies interpretation without a corresponding diagnostic experiment.

E5.justification: Checklist item 7 newly discloses one run per configuration and explains the absence of error bars through computational expense. This is new reporting, not evidence that run counts changed. Neither version supplies confidence intervals or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 5 adds results within the existing LongBench evaluation: on Llama3-8B-Instruct, AsymKV averages 42.32, versus PyramidKV 41.49, SnapKV 41.36, and full context 41.46. These are additional-setting results, not revisions to Llama3.1 performance. The retained tables and plots are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.3.2 adds a quantitative memory-scaling argument: selective gradients require O(cd) additional storage versus O(2ld+p) baseline storage, assuming c is much smaller than l. The key-merging derivation, attention equivalence, and Appendix C proof remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: local key-value asymmetry, training-free asymmetric merging with lossless value representation, and superior benchmark performance. The headline LongBench comparison of 43.95 versus H2O's 38.89 is unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 newly interprets gains over full-context processing as regularization: merging low-attention tokens supposedly suppresses contextual noise. This mechanism explanation is not experimentally isolated. The existing FlashAttention/vLLM compatibility limitation remains unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-access link and documents an Apache 2.0 implementation license, pointing readers to README setup and reproduction instructions. Appendix E also lists existing asset licenses. These are new reproducibility disclosures; repository contents cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds PyramidKV as cited prior work and expands comparative positioning through Appendix D. Most newly evaluated methods were already cited in v1. The additional SnapKV bibliography entry and consolidated KVMerger entries represent existing works, not distinct additions or removals.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence remain intact. Local additions cover memory accounting and regularization, alongside a checklist, acknowledgments, Appendices D–E, and updated affiliation and conference text.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn into three panels with token diagrams, similarity illustrations, and the LMA formula, with a revised caption. Table 5 is added. Other figures and tables are retained, with surrounding text and appendices reflowed.

improvement.justification: Appendix D strengthens competitive evaluation, while the code/license information and explicit single-run disclosure improve transparency. These are useful, limited gains over an otherwise stable paper. The regularization explanation remains untested, and the checklist's assertion that cross-model consistency establishes statistical significance is unsupported by formal uncertainty analysis.
